rc74_released_for: RC74 is the final isolated-staging polish layer after the user-confirmed clean RC73 functional QA. It changes no authentication, attendance storage, reward, Personnel, Speedtest, voice/video, or Firebase authorization behavior. The Attendance selected-agent identity row now uses the existing friendly POD directory label instead of exposing raw tt-custom-pod identifiers, and its avatar/name/POD/edit controls use responsive spacing. Release-package hygiene is cleaned so only current-release handoff files remain at ZIP root while historical RC handoff/regression artifacts are organized under docs/release-history. RC73 Speedtest Write Acknowledgement and all earlier passing fixes are preserved. Firebase RTDB rules are unchanged. Production untouched; isolated staging candidate only. RC73 closes the RC72 real-staging false-503 that remained after a successful secure Speedtest write. Firebase RTDB HTTP success is now the authoritative PUT receipt because firebaseAdminSet throws on non-2xx responses; TrinoTime no longer rejects an already-successful write because Firebase echoed the same JSON with different property ordering or an omitted body. Only an ambiguous failed PUT performs one secure mutation-ID readback, and that readback compares normalized Speedtest records semantically rather than raw JSON serialization. Unverified ambiguous writes still fail closed. RC72/RC71 session continuity, RC70 Rewards Recovery, and RC69 Session Lifecycle are preserved. Firebase RTDB rules are unchanged. Production untouched; isolated staging candidate only. RC72 closes the remaining real-staging Speedtest false-503 case observed after RC71: when secure Personnel storage has actually committed a result but the immediate verification network step is ambiguous, the Worker now verifies Firebase's successful PUT acknowledgement directly and, when the PUT itself fails ambiguously, performs one secure mutation-ID reconciliation before returning an HTTP error. A committed secure result therefore returns success instead of forcing the browser to recover from a false 503. Unverified writes still fail closed. RC71 session continuity, RC70 Rewards Recovery, and RC69 Session Lifecycle are preserved unchanged. Firebase RTDB rules are unchanged. Production untouched; isolated staging candidate only. RC71 hardens the Personnel/Speedtest authority lifecycle observed after RC70 staging QA. An already-valid Agent/TL workforce security token may be rotated near expiry only after the Worker revalidates current roster/POD, active credential state and revocation cutoff; each token remains bounded to the existing 12-hour TTL and an expired/revoked token cannot be resurrected. Automatic Speedtest listener refresh waits for usable workforce authority and resumes on workforce-ready events. Secure Personnel storage remains authoritative, so a transitional legacy /kv mirror outage cannot turn a verified Speedtest commit into a false 503; the client also reconciles an ambiguous 5xx by reading the secure result back. RC70 Rewards Recovery and RC69 Session Lifecycle are preserved. Firebase RTDB rules are unchanged. Production untouched; isolated staging candidate only. RC70 converts post-recovery Attendance Rewards schedule-authority loss from an HTTP 409 into an explicit safe pending state. It preserves the last verified reward summary, permanent earned achievements, claims and equipped cosmetics without writing synthetic zero attendance; it reuses the existing approved schedule migration fallback when available; missing POD schedule data remains pending; expensive Attendance/Leave scans are skipped while schedule authority is absent; and persistent GET-side reward CAS contention degrades to a last-verified pending response while POST reward mutations remain concurrency-protected. The Profile UI renders verification pending instead of misleading zeroed statistics. RC69 session lifecycle is preserved unchanged. Production untouched; isolated staging candidate only. RC69 separates RTDB readiness from Worker role approval and defers governance reads until a signed-in settled session. Live staging acceptance pending. RC66 responds to the real RC65 staging reproduction where a freshly signed-in Team Leader rendered the workspace while Governance had no retained secure workforce authority. Agent/TL login now requires a retained token plus immediate server validation before workspace entry; newly issued sessions are verified server-side; password changes rotate a verified session; persistent UI restoration requires live workforce authority; generic unrelated 401 responses cannot erase the workforce token; and true authority loss triggers one controlled re-auth. RC65 dark-mode Agent Search and RC64 Owner Recovery are preserved. Production untouched; isolated staging candidate only. RC65 closes the post-recovery Agent/Team Leader authority race by binding newly issued workforce sessions to a fresh canonical roster read and retrying a canonical cache miss once before declaring a signed session stale. Genuine authority expiry is centralized client-side, protected polling is suppressed after confirmed expiry, and auth failures do not alter network-health state. Attendance Agent Search dark-mode contrast is corrected without changing light mode. RC64 Owner Recovery and Bio Break Total Duration are preserved. Production untouched; isolated staging candidate only. Existing workforce legacy /kv reads preserved temporarily for compatibility while browser writes remain locked down. RC51 Coaching listener lifecycle remains explicitly preserved and unchanged. RC64 Bio Break Total Duration continues to render hours, minutes, and seconds.
screen_sharing_limitations: Direct calls only; no system/tab audio mixing or recording; both endpoints require RC75 or later. Cross-device staging screen sharing was user-confirmed working; broader browser/TURN/network coverage remains a production-monitoring concern.

Firebase RTDB rules are unchanged. Production untouched. Native picker and authenticated staging acceptance are still required.

rc78_released_for: RC78 fixes the remaining real-browser Team Leader recurring day-off 403 by scoping the browser dayoff_schedule payload to the verified Team Leader home POD before the change is queued or sent. The secure Schedule snapshot may still merge privacy-scoped server data into DEFAULT_SCHEDULE for rendering, but those reconstructed defaults are no longer serialized back as cross-POD edits. RC78 also sanitizes previously queued RC77 dayoff_schedule payloads before replay so stale full/default-filled localStorage entries do not continue the 403 loop. The RC77 Worker own-POD merge and strict cross-POD, backup-TL, and other-TL protections remain unchanged; Admin full-blob behavior remains unchanged. RC76 production cleanup and RC75 user-confirmed cross-device screen sharing are preserved. Firebase RTDB rules are unchanged. Production remains untouched until explicit deployment approval and production configuration preflight. Existing workforce legacy /kv reads preserved temporarily for compatibility while browser writes remain locked down. RC51 Coaching listener lifecycle remains explicitly preserved and unchanged. RC64 Bio Break Total Duration continues to render hours, minutes, and seconds. Production untouched; explicit approval is required before any production deployment. RC77 fixes the real staging Team Leader recurring day-off 403 caused by writing a privacy-scoped own-POD schedule slice as if it were the entire shared dayoff_schedule blob. The Worker now merges the verified Team Leader own-POD slice into the authoritative full schedule server-side, preserves all other PODs unchanged, keeps cross-POD edits forbidden, keeps Admin full-blob behavior unchanged, and scopes TL success/conflict responses so other POD schedules are never disclosed. inherited_released_for: RC88 responds to real-staging RC87 findings. Normal Admin Firebase credentials were confirmed valid, but the recovered staging database is missing that UID's active Admin role. RC88 keeps Firebase password authentication fail-closed: a successful normal Admin credential check may register a short-lived server-verified recovery candidate, and only a fresh verified Owner Recovery session can repair that exact candidate role with read-back confirmation and an audit record. The normal Admin password is not changed.
